stage1.impression: A floating black glossy basin block against vertical timber boards, with a brushed-steel spout and lever and a bar of soap. It reads as a competent CG vanity render rather than a night photograph: the frame is too bright and even for a night room, the wall directly under the slab is the brightest thing in the frame so the block looks pasted on with no contact shadow, the boards are a pinkish-mauve with knots that seem to repeat, and the bowl's underside shows through the front as a pale saucer. As a specific place it reads as a generic hotel or restaurant washroom detail. A magazine would not run it as Planet EARF; at best it would run as a small detail once the fir and the smoked-glass character come through.

blocking_9: The slab casts a soft, believable shadow onto the boards beneath it; the wall under the slab is darker than the wall beside it (now 157 vs 77)
The boards read as honey or amber Douglas fir under 2700 K, not pink or mauve (now r94 g72 b70, so b is close to g)
The Smoke slab reads as smoked glass: a dim, legible reflection gradient and bright polished arrises on the front face, not a flat black void (front median 4.6, 33% crushed)
The bowl interior reads from the camera as a soft lit hollow; the bowl's underside does not show through the front as a pale plastic saucer
No tiling or repeat in the board grain and knots
No unexplained pale blur at the frame edge (the left strip at x 205-235)
Some sign of life and a hint of the rest of the room, so the frame says this bar and not any washroom

defects.what: Overexposed for a night interior: lum_median 85.8, target 22-50
Wall below the floating slab is brightly lit (median 157, brighter than the wall beside it at 77). There is no contact or cast shadow, so the slab looks composited or floating in CG
Boards read pink or mauve (r94 g72 b70) rather than warm fir; reads as stained oak laminate
Knots repeat at near-regular vertical intervals on the board left of the strip, which suggests texture tiling
A pale, defocused vertical strip (median 141) at the left with no readable source; it reads as an artefact or a mis-placed edge
Front face of the Smoke slab is a near-flat black void (median 4.6, crush 33%) with almost no reflection of the room
The bowl underside shows through the front as a pale white saucer shape, which reads as lit plastic or Corian
Bowl interior barely seen from this low eye height; the rim highlight clips (2.2% clipped) while the bowl is crushed (37%)
Walnut-veneer column at the right edge is cut by the frame, pinkish (r126 g95 b95), and its grain looks smeared or stretched at the top
The spout escutcheon highlight clips (3.4%) and reads as chrome CG rather than brushed steel

out_of_scope.request: Show a visible fixing or bracket so the floating slab is plausible
out_of_scope.why: The sink's design (floating off the wall) is fixed by the card; a cast shadow (c2) should carry the plausibility instead.

out_of_scope.request: A faint internal glow in the Smoke slab to separate it from the dark wall
out_of_scope.why: The card rules out internal glow by design (a lit tinted block reads as a lit Corian box).
